title: From “fast and always up” to numbers you can design and test against
captions: A product manager asks for an order status page that is "fast" and "always up". Both words feel clear, but you cannot design or test against them.
You ask who uses the page, how many people use it at the busiest time, and what it costs them when it is slow or down.
"Fast" becomes a percentile at a stated load: 99% of requests answer in under 300 ms, at the dinner peak of 2,000 requests per second.
"Always up" becomes an availability target over a month, with planned maintenance counted as downtime. You also agree how much saved data you may lose in a disaster.
You write each need down with its number, how you will measure it, and who asked for it. The PM agrees. Now each part of the design can point to the need it serves.
